solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former lover having requests cries

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone's ex keeps making demands, and they complain about it loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cries' looks like a noun after 'requests', but here it is a verb: cries out, exclaims.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly.

clue.text: Poet denied king food

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king; it is removed

explanation.surface: A poet is kept from the royal table.
explanation.walkthrough: EATS as a noun is informal for food, as in 'good eats'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal American usage: 'eats' as a plural noun means food, as on a diner sign offering good eats.

clue.text: Fall apart, having cold and noise in stomach?

parts.note: C = cold, as on a tap
a hungry stomach rumbles; the question mark flags the description

explanation.surface: Someone collapses with a chill and an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noise in stomach' is a description, not a synonym, which is why it carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that crumbles breaks into fragments, as old walls or collapsing plans do.

clue.text: Group of coots in Asia flying

indicators.note: the letters scatter as birds do when they take off

parts.note: all eleven letters, 'in' included, are the fodder

explanation.surface: A flock of coots takes wing somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a joining word, but its letters are part of the fodder: COOTS alone is far too short for eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An association is a group of people joined for a purpose.

clue.text: Confused situation with nothing right in church service

indicators.note: 'in' places what comes before it within what follows, so nothing and right sit within the service

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic eucharist service

explanation.surface: A muddle in which nothing goes right during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The service is split M|ASS to take OR between its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is literally a bog, and figuratively a confused, entangling situation.

clue.text: Stylish little bird with tail hidden

indicators.note: the last letter of the bird is concealed, so dropped

parts.note: a chick is a baby bird

explanation.surface: A smart little bird tucks its tail feathers away.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail of a word is its last letter, so CHICK loses its K.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from French: chic describes smart, fashionable dress or taste.

clue.text: Sixty minutes with one beautiful female

parts.note: the unit of time that sixty minutes make up
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An hour spent with a lovely woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A houri is one of the beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise, and by extension any alluring woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Houri has come to mean any voluptuously beautiful woman.

clue.text: Oily liquid ruining eco-store

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone spills a nasty oily liquid all over a green shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Creosote, a tar-oil wood preservative, is about as far from eco-friendly as it gets, which is the surface's irony.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by kind: the tarry preservative painted on fences is a brown oily liquid distilled from coal or wood tar.

clue.text: Trips made by drunkard rolling over outside old city

indicators.note: 'outside' puts the rolled-over drunkard on the outer side of the city, wrapping it

explanation.surface: A drunk tumbles about on a sightseeing trip round an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur of the Chaldees is the crossword's favourite old city. TOS is split TO|S around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tours are trips taken for pleasure or sightseeing.

clue.text: Loner in sports ground, learner needing exercise

parts.note: the rec is a recreation ground, British for a public playing field
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A solitary figure at the playing field, a beginner in need of a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercise' pulls toward physical training, but it means use, as in exercising a right.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse is someone who lives alone and avoids company.

clue.text: Odd creation modified and harmonised

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A strange invention gets tweaked until it all works together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' reads as the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'modified' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Coordinated things are made to work together in harmony.

clue.text: Supports politicians giving accounts of what happened earlier

parts.note: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Party supporters give a history of past events.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads naturally as back + stories, which hides the real break after the S. Tories are Britain's Conservatives, the usual crossword politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstories are the histories that lie behind characters or events.

clue.text: Arrive shortly on flat territory and grumble

indicators.note: COME is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a plain is a flat expanse of land

explanation.surface: A traveller turns up on the flatlands and moans about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon', but it means clip the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to voice discontent, grumbling being the muttering kind.

clue.text: Musical dramas are so fantastic when piano is included

indicators.note: ARE SO is made wild and rearranged

explanation.surface: Operas are wonderful once the piano joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' seems part of the music scene, but it is just P, the musical marking for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by kind: works like Carmen or Tosca are stage plays sung throughout with orchestra.

clue.text: A day given opening — now on calendar?

explanation.surface: Each day brings another door to open on an Advent calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: an Advent calendar is what hangs up now, in the weeks before Christmas, and each day you open a little door. The question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the season before Christmas marked by the Advent calendar.

clue.text: Pill, see, could be this shape

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: Look: a pill might well be oval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This shape' points back to the fodder: many pills are indeed elliptical.
explanation.definitionFit: 'This shape' refers back to the pill: many tablets are oval, the geometric figure the answer names.

clue.text: Go through church under mass of stonework?

parts.note: a pier is a solid masonry support, e.g. for a bridge

explanation.surface: Walking through a church beneath its great stone vaulting.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is standard shorthand. 'Mass' tempts toward the church service, but it is just bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a needle or arrow that pierces passes right through a surface.

clue.text: Temporary pavilion so unstable, sheltering Rex

indicators.note: PAVILION SO is shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A rickety temporary pavilion gives shelter to a man called Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex, Latin for king, gives R, as in the royal signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Provisional means temporary, pending something permanent.

clue.text: Shell of yellow hue on French sea

parts.note: or is gold, yellow, in heraldry

explanation.surface: A yellow-tinted shell lies by the French sea.
explanation.walkthrough: An ormer is an abalone, a shellfish of the Channel Islands; OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is a shellfish, and its ear-shaped shell is prized.

clue.text: Exclamation of annoyance when daughter meets rodent

explanation.surface: A daughter curses on coming across a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: D for daughter is a standard genealogical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild, old-fashioned oath, a softened form of 'God rot', used when something goes wrong.

clue.text: Hospital official who could give Ron meal

indicators.note: the letters could be turned into the answer

explanation.surface: A hospital worker who might hand Ron his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: An almoner was a British hospital social worker, in charge of patients' welfare.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a hospital official dealing with patients' welfare.

clue.text: Candle that a person gets hold of

indicators.note: the words grip the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A candle that someone picks up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a riddle about who holds a candle; the answer is simply inside 'that a person'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by kind: the long thin wax-coated wick used for lighting others is a slender type of candle.

clue.text: Fiddler supposedly with refusal to entertain the Queen

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in your house, so the refusal holds the Queen within

explanation.surface: A violinist says no to playing for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned; 'supposedly' admits the story is legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by legend: the Roman emperor is said to have played while Rome burned in AD 64, a tale historians doubt.

clue.text: Most exciting preliminary contest involving fantastic side

indicators.note: 'involving' in its old sense of enfolding or wrapping up, so the contest encloses the rearranged side

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying round

explanation.surface: The most thrilling qualifier features a remarkable team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' reads as a sports team, fitting the surface, but it is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Heady means intoxicating or exciting, so headiest is most exciting.
